title: 5 Feelings You Shouldn’t Always Trust
paragraphs:
Your heart can feel loud.
But loud doesn’t mean Lord.
Some feelings speak with urgency… and still lie to your soul.
Here are 5 feelings you shouldn’t always trust:

1. “I feel like God has left me.”
Feelings can make abandonment feel real.
But Scripture says, “I will never leave you nor forsake you” (Hebrews 13:5).
God’s presence is not measured by your mood.

2. “I feel condemned, so I must be disqualified.”
Conviction draws you back.
Condemnation drives you into hiding.
Romans 8:1 says, “There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.”
If you belong to Jesus, shame does not get the final word.

3. “I feel like giving in, so it must be what I really want.”
Not every craving is truth.
Not every desire deserves a throne.
Your flesh can beg for what will destroy your peace.
Freedom is not found in feeding every urge. It is found in surrendering to Christ.

4. “I feel strong, so I must be safe.”
That’s dangerous.
Peter felt bold hours before he denied Jesus.
Self-confidence without dependence on God is a setup for collapse.
“Let anyone who thinks that he stands take heed lest he fall” (1 Corinthians 10:12).

5. “I feel hopeless, so nothing can change.”
That one has buried many people before their breakthrough.
But feelings are not prophets.
Jesus still raises what sin crushed, what grief drained, and what failure shamed.
What feels dead to you is not beyond resurrection to Him.

God never told us to be led by feelings.
He told us to be transformed by truth.

Feelings are real.
They are just not always reliable.

This is why we need more than vibes, more than instincts, more than emotional impulse.
We need the Word.
We need the cross.
We need Jesus.

Because without Christ, feelings can turn into idols.
But in Christ, even broken emotions can be brought into healing, order, and obedience.

So when your heart panics, preaches fear, or romanticizes sin, don’t just ask,
“What do I feel?”
Ask,
“What has God said?”
That question can save your life.

Jesus is still truth when your feelings are confused.
Jesus is still grace when your feelings accuse you.
Jesus is still Lord when your emotions are out of control.

Don’t bow to every feeling.
Bring every feeling to the feet of Christ.
